perspective:
Sara’s accessible perspective:

- Sara is a Speech-Language Pathologist; Shirley is her long-time nurse colleague and close friend at a community health center.
- A mutual patient died. Sara attended the funeral and saw Shirley looking somber; Sara suspected Shirley was deeply affected.
- At the funeral, Sara told Shirley she knew it was hard and had seen how much Shirley cared. Shirley said it had been tough and she kept thinking if more could have been done. Sara replied they did everything they could and should remember the good care and joy they brought. Shirley agreed but said it was hard to let go.
- At a work coffee break, Sara raised the patient’s treatment decisions because she sensed Shirley felt burdened. Shirley said she felt responsible and wondered if pushing for a different approach might have helped. Sara said they made the best decisions with the information they had and that the burden was too heavy to carry alone. Shirley appreciated it but said it was hard to accept.
- Later, Sara observed Shirley remained reserved and minimally expressive. In a quiet office moment, Sara told Shirley she noticed she was holding back feelings and it was okay to be open. Shirley said she did not want to seem unprofessional or weak. Sara said expressing emotions is not weak and is healthy among friends. Shirley said maybe Sara was right and she would try to be more open.
- Sara later felt her confrontation might have been too harsh and apologized if she came on too strong. Shirley said it was a bit much but knew Sara meant well and appreciated the apology. Sara said she was there for Shirley however needed. Shirley thanked her and said they should keep talking; it helps.
- After some time, Sara noticed Shirley seemed improved and felt hopeful. Sara asked how Shirley was feeling. Shirley said she felt better thanks to their talks and Sara’s support. Sara offered to spend more time together outside work. Shirley agreed and suggested planning something for the weekend.
